facts.text: MOVES maps action 0 to up, 1 to down, 2 to left and 3 to right, and the action space is Discrete(4)
The observation space is Discrete(nrow * ncol), one integer per grid cell
An observation is the flattened cell index row * ncol + col
A grid cell is free when it holds 0 and an obstacle when it holds 1
GridModel.is_free returns False for a cell outside the grid
A step moves the agent to the target cell when it is in bounds and free, and leaves it in place otherwise
The reward is +1.0 on the goal, -0.1 for a valid non-goal cell and -1.0 for an invalid move
The episode terminates when the agent reaches the goal
The episode truncates when step_count is at least max_steps and the goal was not reached on that step
step returns (observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info)
The reset info carries agent_xy and step_count
reset(seed) calls super().reset(seed=seed), so the sampled positions come from the environment's numpy generator
A reset without a start_loc or goal_loc option samples a free cell with GridModel.sample_valid_xy
The start_loc and goal_loc options accept a flat integer index or a (row, col) pair, and an invalid start or goal raises ValueError
SimpleGrid-4x4-v0 is registered with entry point gym_simplegrid.envs:SimpleGridEnv, kwargs obstacle_map=MAP_4x4 and max_episode_steps=200
MAP_4x4 has four rows of four cells: 0000, 0101, 0001 and 1000
The environment declares the render modes human, rgb_array and ansi with render_fps 8

determinism.notes: reset(seed) seeds the environment's numpy generator (simple_grid.py:68) and the sampled start and goal (simple_grid.py:167-168); after that the grid transition is deterministic, and cap.world.seed.v1 supplies the seed of the next reset.  The fake draws those positions with Python's random.Random instead of numpy's Generator, so one seed gives different positions on the two.  The environment has no time base: timestep_ms is 0 and every cap.world.step.v1 tick is one state transition.

gaps: F0: the environment is a discrete grid state machine with no dynamics: no forces, contacts, friction, actuator, sensor or noise model, and a step changes the cell directly
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and timestep_ms 0, so only commands advance the state and no simulated time passes
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

the fake backend is a pure-Python re-implementation of the clone's state machine; it samples the start and goal with Python's random.Random while upstream samples them from numpy's generator (simple_grid.py:68 and :167-168), so one seed gives different positions on the two, and it was not compared with the upstream environment

the fake models the 200-step TimeLimit that gymnasium.make adds to SimpleGrid-4x4-v0 (gym_simplegrid/__init__.py:31) itself, because the bridge drives an environment object and does not call gymnasium.make; the upstream SimpleGridEnv class alone does not truncate when max_steps is None
snapshot and restore are not offered: SimpleGridEnv exposes no get_state or set_state
rendering is not exposed: the environment's human, rgb_array and ansi modes (simple_grid.py:20 and :116-128) need matplotlib, and cap.world.render.v1 is unbound

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
